_meta.indication: PYRUKYND is indicated for the treatment of hemolytic anemia in adults with pyruvate kinase (PK) deficiency.

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; mitapivat titrated up to 50 mg twice daily vs placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: 80 adults with PK deficiency who were not regularly transfused (no more than 4 transfusions in prior 52 weeks and none in prior 3 months).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Hb response, defined as a >=1.5 g/dL increase in Hb from baseline sustained at 2 or more scheduled assessments (Weeks 16, 20, and 24) during the fixed-dose period without transfusions.
pivotal_trials.n: N=80 total; efficacy analysis PYRUKYND N=40, placebo N=40 (safety population placebo N=39).
pivotal_trials.result: Hb response: 16 (40%) with PYRUKYND vs 0 with placebo; difference 39% (95% CI 24, 55); p<0.0001.

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational single-arm, open-label trial; dose optimization to 50 mg twice daily followed by 24-week fixed-dose period.
pivotal_trials.population: 27 adults with PK deficiency who were regularly transfused (minimum of 6 transfusion episodes in the prior 52-week period).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Transfusion reduction response, defined as >=33% reduction in the number of RBC units transfused during the fixed-dose period compared with the patient's historical transfusion burden.
pivotal_trials.result: Transfusion reduction response in 9 (33%) patients (95% CI 17, 54); 6 (22%) patients were transfusion free (95% CI 9, 42).

key_safety: The most common adverse reactions including laboratory abnormalities (>=10%) were estrone decreased (males), increased urate, back pain, estradiol decreased (males), and arthralgia. In ACTIVATE, back pain occurred in 15% (PYRUKYND) vs 8% (placebo) and arthralgia in 10% vs 5%. Estrone decreased in 56.3% of males on PYRUKYND vs 0 on placebo.
target_moa: Mitapivat is a first-in-class pyruvate kinase activator that allosterically binds the PK-R tetramer, increasing PK activity to elevate intracellular ATP, improve RBC energy homeostasis, prolong RBC lifespan and reduce hemolysis.
modality: Small molecule (mitapivat sulfate, an oral pyruvate kinase activator)

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held; the application did not raise safety or effectiveness issues requiring external expert advice.

summary.text: Mitapivat, a first-in-class pyruvate kinase activator and new molecular entity, received orphan drug designation in March 2015 and Fast-Track Designation for PKD, and was reviewed under the priority review timeline. It was approved via the traditional (non-accelerated) pathway as the first product for PK deficiency, without an advisory committee.

requirement.text: Complete Trial AG-348-C-011, an open-label, multicenter extension study of AG-348 in adults with PKD previously enrolled in AG-348 studies (final report to include long-term AEs including reproductive hormones, blood lipids, bone fractures).

citations.quote: 4178-1 Complete Trial AG-348-C-011, "An Open-Label, Multicenter, Extension Study of AG-348 in Adult Subjects With Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency Previously Enrolled in AG-348 Studies." The final study report must include patient level data and a summary of all adverse events including changes in reproductive hormones, changes in blood lipids, bone fractures and other adverse events associated with long-term aromatase inhibition.
